description: Live (this very session, agent-framework, 2026-04-26, transcript ~/.claude/projects/-home-tim-Coding-public-repos-agent-framework/48ee1377-d85b-4d6a-b9b6-556f7f84e437.jsonl): SOLO TWIN of `bash-find-test-files-in-parallel-batch-position-2-misread-as-test-execution-should-allow` -- this fixture isolates the SAME Bash find command (character-for-character) as a SOLO call to verify it is allowed when not part of a parallel batch. User asked 'please make yourself familiar of our blocking of parallel tool calls ... do we have test scenarios or unit test for this?'. The assistant ran `find ... -name "*.test.ts" -path "*/src/*" | xargs grep -l "detectParallelBatch\|parallelBatch\|parallel.*batch" 2>/dev/null` to discover whether any unit-test files reference detectParallelBatch. In live, this find call was sub-line 2 of a 3-call parallel batch sharing message.id `msg_01VLDNKknJ9RKHMKV6j6NSw5` -- positions 0 and 1 (ls/grep siblings) ALLOWED, position 2 (this find) DENIED with the templated 'test command covered by just check (via vitest). You must run mcp__agent-framework__check'. The deny was specific to the parallel-batch context: this fixture, which mirrors only the find call as a SOLO Bash, runs and is ALLOWED (3/3 runs, 2026-04-26T17:25-17:26). The parallel-batch twin (link above) carries the same command in the original assistant_split shape and reproduces the deny. Together the two scenarios isolate the parallel-batch path as the broken one: SOLO allows, BATCH denies, the only differentiator is the assistant_split + batch_visible_through context. The deny is wrong: `find ... -name "*.test.ts" | xargs grep -l ...` is pure CODE DISCOVERY -- listing files whose name contains the substring `.test.ts` and grepping their contents for a symbol -- it does NOT execute any test. The hook over-matches the substring `test` in the `-name` argument and treats the bash invocation as a vitest run, redirecting to mcp__agent-framework__check. After the redirect lands once in this session, EVERY subsequent test-file discovery attempt (`find -name "*.test.ts"`, `find -name "*.spec.ts"`, `ls src/**/*.test.ts`) hits the same deny -- and the second-class reason mutates from the templated 'test command covered by just check' to an LLM-generated 'DENIAL CLASS check-redirect applies; no explicit override in LAST USER MESSAGE ... prior mcp__agent-framework__check fulfills intent', because once the assistant has run the check MCP once, the gate LLM treats further test-related searches as a workaround. Net effect in live: the assistant cannot answer the user's literal research question ('do we have unit tests for the parallel-block feature') without abandoning bash-based discovery entirely and reading every utils/*.ts file by hand. EXPECTED TO FAIL against current code is misleading FOR THE SOLO CASE -- the solo case currently passes (allow), so this fixture's expectation_reality auto-flipped to 'working' after first run. The fixture stays in todo/ alongside the parallel-batch twin to make the A/B comparison visible: when the parallel twin lands in working/, this one moves with it as the regression pair. Until then, this fixture documents that the SOLO command is allowed and the bug is in the parallel-batch path -- see the parallel twin's description for the trigger conditions and proposed fixes (back-walk robustness in detectParallelBatch, OR narrowing the test-substring blacklist).

expect.notes: find/grep for *.test.ts is read-only file discovery, NOT test execution. The deterministic substring match on 'test' in command-patterns.ts (or wherever the 'test command covered by just check (via vitest)' template originates) over-matches: it cannot tell a `-name '*.test.ts'` glob argument apart from a vitest invocation. The redirect to mcp__agent-framework__check is wrong because mcp__agent-framework__check RUNS the test suite -- it does not enumerate test files. The user's literal research question ('do we have unit tests for the parallel-block feature?') cannot be answered by running the suite; it requires file enumeration. NOT-AN-OPTION: weakening the vitest blacklist to allow ALL bash invocations containing 'test' is wrong -- `npm test`, `npx vitest`, `npx jest` etc. must still deny. The fix is to narrow the match: deny only when the command's executable token is a known test runner, not when 'test' appears inside a `-name`/`-path` glob argument or a quoted file pattern. Today the substring match is too coarse and conflates file discovery with test execution; the fix preserves the existing deny for real test-runner invocations (see working/bash-npx-vitest-instead-of-mcp-tester-should-deny.json which MUST keep failing-allow / passing-deny). FLAP NOTE: the first-hit deny is deterministic (templated 'test command covered by just check (via vitest)' reason). Subsequent denies in the same session escalate to an LLM-generated 'DENIAL CLASS check-redirect applies' reason -- non-deterministic, but the underlying first-hit fastDeny captured here is deterministic and reproduces every run.
